scope: DERIVED from model FLOPs and forced operand traffic. NOT HBM-measured. bw_lb_gbps = minimum effective traffic rate to achieve the observed device time; utilization_vs_peak compares MODEL effective TFLOP/s to the repo reference peak, it is NOT a matrix-unit counter activity.
hardware_status: unverified (PCM BLOCKED - no HBM bytes / matrix-unit activity)
bw_lb_caveat: bw_lb_gbps = forced_bytes_lb / device_ms. It assumes each operand byte is moved once per call with NO on-chip reuse; per-shape values of 1e5 GB/s exceed any HBM and are therefore a FORMAL lower-bound artifact, not an achieved/required HBM bandwidth. Real HBM traffic needs PCM counters (BLOCKED).
critical_path_method: per step: window=[first marker start, next step start); busy = UNION of clipped kernel+memcpy+memset intervals (NOT a sum of durations); idle=window-busy; overlap=|K|+|M|-|K u M|

conclusion.situation_1_compute_efficiency_low: backward GEMM hotspots run at 88.1-129.25 TFLOP/s = 63%-93% of the 139.2 reference -> 7%-37% headroom vs reference; kernel tuning space EXISTS but is bounded (<=~37% of the 772 ms backward GEMM = <=~285 ms theoretical ceiling, realistically far less)
conclusion.situation_2_forced_traffic: dW arithmetic intensity 656-706 FLOP/byte -> STRONGLY COMPUTE-BOUND (AI is far above any roofline knee; a bf16 GEMM at 2765 GB/s HBM and 139 TFLOP/s has its knee at ~50 FLOP/byte). The per-shape bw_lb_gbps (1.2e5-2.3e5 GB/s) is NOT physically meaningful as an HBM requirement: it assumes every operand byte is fetched once per call with no cache reuse across the 96 calls of the step, whereas weights/activations are reused via on-chip caches. It is reported only as the formal lower-bound formula value and MUST NOT be read as an achieved or required HBM bandwidth.
conclusion.situation_2_contiguous_copy: the .contiguous() copy FlagGems mm performs on a transposed A adds 8053.06 MB (S=512 dW-up) and 2013.27 MB (S=512 dW-down) of extra read+write per shape per step - a real extra traffic item, counted SEPARATELY from the GEMM body; it is why native+contiguous() loses (+32.4 ms median) while FlagGems still gains (its Triton kernel is faster on the contiguous operand by more than the copy costs)
conclusion.situation_3_idle_large: per-step idle 211-250 ms (87.9-91.5% busy) - idle is 8%-12% of the step and is NOT attributable without a host swimlane (needs counters/platform)
conclusion.ranking: backward GEMM (38%) > backward attention (18.5%) > forward GEMM (16.2%) > forward attention (10.1%)
conclusion.direction: (a) backward GEMM (38%) has the largest absolute headroom but its effective TFLOP/s (88-129) is already 63%-93% of reference -> vendor-side kernel tuning, not application-level; the transposed-view dW shapes (88 TF/s, 63%) are the weakest - a vendor fast path for transposed operands would target ~27 ms/step of the 258 ms dW time at most; (b) attention (fwd+bwd ~28.6%) runs at 12-13 TFLOP/s model-math over STAGE time - NOT comparable to the GEMM peak (softmax/dropout/masking are inside the stage time) -> needs a training-capable SDPA candidate (FlagGems ruled out); (c) idle 8-12% (211-250 ms/step) -> submission gaps or exposed copies, NOT attributable without a host swimlane
conclusion.platform_assistance: PCM window (pg-exporter), equivalent counter tool, vendor confirmation of metric level - see hbm_blocked_r46.md
